## Occupancy legality (the make-or-break check)
- Zone **RX-5** under Charlottesville's 2024 Development Code → **by-the-room renting to
  unrelated students is legal**; the code removed unrelated-occupant caps citywide.
- ⚠️ **Stability flag:** the 2024 code was litigated (*White v. City of Charlottesville*),
  briefly voided mid-2025, **settled Oct 2025 and back in effect.** Confirm currency and
  pull a fresh per-parcel zoning determination before closing.
- **By-room is permitted here** → underwrite the higher-yield model.

---

## Underwriting (modeled over the real $1,077,800 value; all-cash)
Assumptions: student rent ~$850/bed; Charlottesville real-estate tax 0.96% of assessed;
mgmt 10%; vacancy 12% (student summer gap); purchase at assessed-value proxy (real price
negotiated). **Bed/unit count is modeled — confirm via Residential Details layer.**

**By-the-room (headline) — modeled 8 beds:**
- Gross: 8 × $850 × 12 = **$81,600/yr**
- Opex ≈ $38,300 (tax $10,347 · ins $4,000 · maint $6,000 · mgmt $8,160 · vacancy $9,792)
- **NOI ≈ $43,300 → cap rate / cash-on-cash ≈ 4.0%**

**Whole-building — modeled ~3 units @ ~$1,850/mo:**
- Gross ≈ $66,600/yr → NOI ≈ $34,300 → **≈ 3.1%**

→ By-room is the better legal model here (+0.9 pts of yield). Both are *thin* — see the
strategic note.

## Financing recommendation 💵
**Recommended: Cash / conventional (DSCR).**
- The owner **bought for $1.0M in May 2024** at ~current value → **low capital-gains
  exposure** and a **2024-vintage loan ≈ market rate**, so neither seller-finance nor a
  Subject-To rate gap offers an edge. All-cash gives you speed/certainty leverage.

**Subject-To — SUPPRESSED.** Reason: recent arm's-length purchase, **mortgage balance
unverified**, and **no rate gap** to exploit. The engine will not force creative finance
where the signals don't support it.

**Seller finance — unlikely.** A buyer two years in with little gain has weak motivation
to carry paper; revisit only if owner circumstances change.

> If any creative structure *were* triggered, it would ship with its legal guardrail
> (due-on-sale, Dodd-Frank/SAFE, the Garn-St.-Germain trust caveat) and an attorney
> trigger — see `docs/financing-engine-design.md`. None apply here.

## Risks & what to verify before acting
- **Thin cap rate (~4%)** — typical of the prime block; sensitive to rent and vacancy.
- **Unit/bed count is modeled** — pull the Residential Details layer (real beds/units)
  before trusting the pro-forma.
- **Rents are modeled** — get real per-bedroom student comps near grounds.
- **Condition/age** — 1983-era ownership history; budget capex; inspect.
- **Student vacancy** — budget the summer gap / consider 12-month or by-bed leases.
- **Zoning currency** — reconfirm RX-5 by-room post-settlement.

## Strategic note (the judgment that matters)
1301 Wertland is a **real, legal, walk-to-grounds by-room property** — but at ~$1.08M for
~4% it's priced like the institutional multifamily it sits next to (1207-11 Wertland is
assessed $9.9M at ~1.7% cap). **Your edge isn't the trophy block; it's by-room-eligible
single-family a few blocks off-prime, which pencils ~5%+ for a fraction of the capital.**
Treat 1301 as a benchmark, not necessarily the buy.

## Verdict
**Watch / benchmark.** Strong location and clean legality, but thin yield and low seller
motivation. Pursue only if you can buy meaningfully below assessed value or confirm a
higher real bed count. **Next:** pull Residential Details + rent comps to harden the
numbers, and run the off-prime SFR shortlist for comparison.
